PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve remote agent and resource URI identities
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341705.

## Summary

The editor-remote connection advertises custom agents using workbench `vscode-remote:` URIs, but selected-agent URIs were not translated back to host-local identities when sending a message. The host therefore failed to match a selected remote custom agent and used its default agent instead.

- Map selected agents in initial messages, turns, drafts, queued/steering messages, loaded history, and snapshot/reconnect state.
- Translate same-host resource attachments on send, without rewriting client-owned attachments echoed by the host.
- Project resource and skill completions through the owning connection's resource mapper, and unwrap resource attachments only when they belong to that connection.
- Preserve unrelated authorities, built-in/provider agent identities, query/fragment data, and opaque protocol metadata.

This PR contains only the URI fixes and their regression tests. Bootstrap/module-loader changes are excluded.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --grep "EditorRemoteAgentHostTransport|AgentHostChatContribution (request attachments|provideChatInputCompletions)" --reporter dot` — **passed, 57 tests**, including after rebasing onto current main and after the CI formatting correction.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.ts src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\agentHostSessionHandler.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed, four files**.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` — **passed**.
- `node build\hygiene.ts src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.ts src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\agentHostSessionHandler.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed, four files**, after fixing the completion test formatting flagged by the first CI run.
- Reused the existing client compilation/watch output; `.build\log` reports **zero diagnostics**. Tests ran with the bootstrap edits removed and baseline bootstrap output rebuilt by the watcher.

Live WSL/model-provider verification has not been run. To verify manually, open a WSL workspace, select a custom copy of Ask from the remote user's agents directory, and request a file creation. The custom agent's read-only instructions should be honored just like built-in Ask. Also check file/folder/selection attachments and resource/skill completions on the remote connection.

## Review follow-up validation

- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\common\editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --reporter dot` — **passed, 877 tests** across both complete suites, including the restored-message resend assertion and remote worktree ownership regressions.
- Three new remote worktree rebasing cases **failed before the fix** with original-checkout paths; all pass after the fix.
- Changed-file `node build\hygiene.ts` and `npm run eslint --` — **passed** for all three corrected files.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — **failed locally on SDK/node-pty dependency mismatches outside this PR** (`fusionTier` and `setParentWindow`); the PR's snapshot-fixture type error is fixed. Clean CI compilation passed for the first follow-up; the latest native-remote follow-up is being monitored.
Native remote follow-up: registered WSL and SSH handlers now normalize their explicitly owned native remote authority before rebasing and host-addressability filtering. Four additional native-remote cases (host-form and client-form resolved directories, including authority casing and client/foreign-resource preservation) were verified failing before the fix and passing afterward. Changed-file hygiene and ESLint passed for the handler, editor contribution wiring, and tests. Bootstrap edits remain excluded.
<sub>Written by Connor's agent</sub>

Scenarios.Scenario: Send or synchronize a remote-agent chat message with selected-agent and resource attachments, including draft, queued, steering, and initial messages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The handler converts input variables and rebases attachment URIs, then EditorRemoteAgentHostTransport synchronously projects selected-agent/resource identities before the existing protocol send. Turn submission waits for this projection; draft publication is coalesced by a 500 ms per-session Delayer before reaching the same send path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the JSON-RPC createChat or dispatchAction protocol message over the existing agent-host transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing transport send per create-chat/action after draft coalescing; attachments are grouped inside that message, so A attachments do not cause A boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same createChat/dispatchAction message crossed the transport once, but selected-agent and resource-attachment URI fields were not projected by this adapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single existing send is required for the host to receive the message; the new URI work executes synchronously immediately before it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A resource attachments in the message and D requested/workspace directories used for ownership/rebase checks; effective work is in-memory O(A*D) in the existing attachment conversion/rebase path plus O(A) transport projection. Typical D is the workspace-root count, and one transport message is emitted per dispatched action, not per attachment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turn/queue actions issue one dispatch each. Draft edits are last-value coalesced per session over 500 ms, so typing does not dispatch per keystroke. The diff adds no Promise.all, worker, subprocess, or per-attachment concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: URI projection is deterministic and uncached; cold and warm behavior are the same. There is no negative-cache state or repeated remote lookup to coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, 500 ms draft debounce, attachment loops, mapper implementation, and single transport send are explicit in the inspected code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment and multi-root counts vary, but the added mapper work is shallow URI parsing/transformation and object copying; no evidence shows counts or costs large enough to create input latency beyond the already more substantial attachment conversion and serialization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff adds bounded in-memory identity projection without per-attachment boundary fan-out, and draft coalescing prevents per-keystroke repetition.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize, subscribe, reconnect, or load older history for remote chat sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing transport response/action is received and synchronously mapped before subscribers can consume it. The diff now projects selected-agent URIs across loaded turns, active/draft/pending messages, and reconnect replay actions; history refresh then performs its existing full state-to-history conversion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive initialize, subscribe, reconnect, or fetch-history protocol data from the agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing response per request, or one existing server action per loaded history page/replay batch; the diff does not add requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshots, replay envelopes, and history actions crossed the boundary; directory-bearing snapshot fields were mapped, while selected-agent message fields were left untouched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mapping occurs after bytes arrive and before the response/action is emitted to consumers, so its linear CPU cost is on hydration/reconnect/history-load latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N turns in the loaded snapshot/page or replay and P pending messages; added CPU/allocation is O(N+P), with one shallow turn/message copy per loaded turn. Work is bounded by the history already present in the protocol payload.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Incoming protocol messages are delivered through the transport event path and mapped synchronously per message. The diff introduces no concurrent requests or burst; replay/snapshot arrays are traversed once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Snapshots and replay actions are mapped when received and are not cached by this adapter. Cold initialize and reconnect perform the same per-payload mapping; steady-state streaming deltas do not remap the entire turn history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all response/action branches and array traversals are explicit, and there are no transitive filesystem, subprocess, database, or additional network operations in the mapper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long loaded histories increase shallow allocations, but the same payload is already deserialized and subsequently converted into full chat history. No repository evidence establishes that these added shallow copies materially affect hydration or reconnect latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable regression. The new cost is a single linear pass required to project identities in already-loaded data, with no retained duplicate state or repeated full-history pass on streaming updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request remote resource and skill completions while typing in chat input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Monaco invokes completion only while the cursor is inside a host-announced trigger token. One existing agent-host completions request must finish, then each returned item is synchronously converted; the diff wraps resource/skill URIs through the owning connection before suggestions are returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request completion items from the agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing host request per eligible Monaco completion invocation; returned R items are mapped locally with zero per-item boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single completions request returned the same items, which were already iterated and converted; resource and skill URIs were parsed but not additionally wrapped through the owning connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing request dominates the asynchronous critical path; URI wrapping runs after it and before suggestions render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R completion items returned by the host; added URI wrapping is O(R) only for resource and skill items, after effective result cardinality is established by the host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The completion provider uses Monaco cancellation and drops stale results after the await. The token is not forwarded across IPC, so underlying overlap is pre-existing; the diff neither adds requests nor changes concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No completion cache is used on this path; cold and warm requests both delegate to the host. The URI mapping is local and has no cache miss behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the completion provider trigger guard, cancellation check, single connection call, and local result loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host result sizes and request durations vary, but only small per-item serialization/allocation is added and there is no evidence of a realistically large result set making it material.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff preserves one boundary call and adds only linear local projection to the existing result conversion loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a registered native-remote handler and rebase same-authority WSL/SSH attachments into a resolved worktree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Handler registration stores the editor remote authority. On turn construction, each attachment and requested/resolved directory is checked with in-memory resource mappers and authority comparison before the existing message dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the completed turn action to the agent host after all attachments have been rebased
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing message dispatch after all attachments are grouped; zero filesystem, database, subprocess, or per-attachment remote calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Attachment rebasing already ran during turn construction and the grouped action was dispatched once; the diff broadens local ownership normalization to connection-wrapped and same-authority native-remote URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local URI checks precede the existing dispatch but do not add a boundary or await.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A attachments and D candidate working directories; effective cardinality remains one final chat action, with local ownership/rebase checks scaling with A and D rather than boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Attachment conversion is synchronous and sequential during one turn build. The final dispatch retains existing connection sequencing; no new parallelism or resource burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ownership checks are uncached and deterministic. Cold/warm behavior is identical, and no filesystem existence lookup or remote-resolution cache is consulted.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mapper implementations are pure URI encode/decode operations, and all inspected rebase callers run during attachment conversion without I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-root workspaces or unusually attachment-heavy prompts increase local comparisons, but typical root/attachment cardinalities are modest and no concrete latency mechanism beyond bounded CPU/allocation is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added native-remote ownership checks are pure local work and preserve grouped transport behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. The change adds URI projection and shallow copies on message, completion, snapshot, replay, and attachment-rebase paths, but introduces no subprocess/filesystem/database/network boundary, no boundary fan-out, no unbounded retention, and no concurrency burst. Draft traffic is explicitly debounced, and the remaining linear work is bounded by data already serialized or iterated on the same path, so no high-confidence performance finding was submitted.
